summary.short: Requires network operators in China to report cybersecurity incidents to designated authorities within deadlines of 1 to 4 hours for initial reports, depending on operator type and incident grade. Provides an incident classification guide and requires a post-incident summary report within 30 days. Effective 1 November 2025.
summary.long: Issued by the Cyberspace Administration of China on 11 September 2025, in force from 1 November 2025 (Art. 14). Applies to network owners, managers and service providers in China (Arts. 2, 12). Operators must classify incidents under the attached Guide and report larger-grade or higher incidents: critical information infrastructure operators to the protection authority and public security within 1 hour; central state organs to their cyberspace bodies within 2 hours; other operators to the provincial cyberspace authority within 4 hours; major incidents are escalated to the national authority within 30 minutes or 1 hour (Art. 4). Operators must require contracted service providers to report incidents (Art. 5). Reports must cover specified content, including ransom details for ransomware, with supplementary reports as facts emerge (Art. 7). A post-incident summary report is due within 30 days (Art. 8). Non-reporting is penalised under other laws; aggravated penalties apply where late, missed, false or concealed reports cause serious harm (Art. 10). Operators with reasonable protective measures may receive lighter treatment (Art. 11). The Guide sets four grades with quantitative criteria.
